findings.text: This portion contributes many self-checking entries to a shared test table covering arithmetic, logic, shift, jump, and atomic-memory behavior. Each entry pairs a descriptive label with either an inline instruction sequence or a generator callback, plus execution attributes and an expected outcome, allowing a runner to execute the entries without further source context.

A test entry carries a label, an inline or generated program body, a mode marker distinguishing internal execution with an optional no-packet-data flag, empty input descriptors, a small expected result pair, and optionally a stack reservation, a program generator reference, and a repeat count for pattern-sensitive cases.

Atomic-memory coverage spans two operand widths and four update families: plain read-modify-write, fetch-augmented read-modify-write, exchange, and compare-and-exchange. Both widths exercise arithmetic and logical updates, and each width repeats the full family so width handling and fetch semantics are tested symmetrically.

Atomic cases encode a non-clobber contract for uninvolved registers. The program preloads distinct small values into the general registers, performs one stack-relative atomic update, then conditionally checks each register for its preloaded value and reports success only when all comparisons pass.

Thirty-two-bit arithmetic and word-sized atomic updates must preserve the upper half of source registers rather than zero-extending in place. Checks load distinctive wide patterns, apply one narrow operation, then subtract, shift, and combine halves so any upper-bit disturbance yields nonzero while preservation yields zero.

Thirty-two-bit conditional branches must leave full-width operands untouched. Both immediate-operand and register-operand forms are exercised across equality, inequality, bit-test, unsigned ordered, and signed ordered conditions, each followed by an arithmetic reduction that collapses any bit change into the exit value.

Arithmetic and logic coverage is organized by width, operand kind, and operation. Sixty-four-bit and thirty-two-bit families each test immediate-operand variants across destination registers and register-operand variants across source-destination pairs for moves, bitwise logic, shifts, addition, subtraction, multiplication, unsigned division and remainder, with signed division variants for immediate forms.

Shift and magnitude behavior is tested exhaustively rather than by single examples. Dedicated entries iterate over all shift distances for logical and arithmetic shifts in immediate and register forms, including same-register aliasing, and over all immediate and register magnitude classes, with magnitude cases requesting multiple pattern runs and marking that no packet data is needed.

Per-operation generator callbacks serve as deferred entry points invoked by the harness to synthesize programs for register, shift-distance, and magnitude combinations. The table stores only a reference to the relevant builder, so the concrete instruction stream is produced at run time instead of being enumerated statically.

Word and double-word atomic checks reserve eight bytes of stack for the update target, and outcome expectations use a two-integer pair where zero-zero denotes a preservation check expecting no difference and zero-one denotes a functional check expecting success.
